Carry study · Drawing → pattern → body

The Patternmaker Behind the Designer

The patternmaker is not a neutral copying machine: pattern work carries design intention into geometry, fit, construction, repeatability, and the body through skilled decisions that deserve explicit evidence, authority, and credit.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

Fashion mythology often lets a sketch travel directly to a finished garment. Patternmaking occupies the consequential middle. FIT’s current program description names draping, marker making, patternmaking, sample making, knowledge, craftsmanship, and techniques. Its archived 1995 oral history preserves three patternmaking professors discussing slopers, specialized instruction, technology, union history, and long ties to textile work. These sources establish patternmaking as a skilled field; they do not tell us who controlled any private workroom or who legally authored a particular garment.

The V&A’s accounts of Cristóbal Balenciaga and Alexander McQueen make a second, carefully bounded point: pattern cutting was part of those designers’ own training and practice. That history complicates any fixed opposition between “designer” and “patternmaker.” In one house the founder may cut; in another, a specialist may translate, challenge, or co-develop the form. The correct institutional question is not who usually does it, but which person made which decision, from what brief, with what authority, and where that knowledge now lives.

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · BRIEF

What is the design asking the pattern to do?

Record silhouette, balance, ease, movement, material behavior, size range, construction, finish, cost, time, accessibility, and the non-negotiable visual idea. A sketch alone rarely carries all of this.

PROPOSALS73S74

02 · JUDGMENT

Which decisions belong to the patternmaker?

Log the alteration, reason, evidence, person deciding, person approving, affected sizes and materials, and whether the change is technical, aesthetic, safety-related, or commercial. Skilled translation should remain attributable.

INFERENCES72S73

03 · FIT

Whose body becomes the standard?

Identify the block, fit model or measurement source, sample size, grading method, movement test, wearer feedback, and excluded bodies. A technically repeatable pattern can still institutionalize a narrow body assumption.

PROPOSALS72S73

04 · RETAIN

Can the knowledge survive the specialist’s absence?

Preserve pattern version, annotation, toile images where permitted, fitting decisions, known failures, material constraints, maker credit, access rules, and a route for future questions. The file is evidence; narration explains the judgment.

PROPOSALS08S39S72

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

Calling patternmaking authorship can illuminate judgment but also blur distinct legal categories or erase sewing, fitting, grading, textile, and production labor. The answer is not to replace one hero with another. It is to make the chain of contribution and decision precise.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Select one garment and pair the approved sketch, first pattern, first toile, fitting record, production pattern, and final object.
  2. Interview the patternmaker about three changes that are invisible in the finished photograph.
  3. Record who proposed, tested, approved, rejected, and documented each change.
  4. Audit fit assumptions, size coverage, credit, compensation, file custody, reuse, and succession with the actual participants.

PACKAGE SYSTEM

One inquiry, six publishing forms

  • Canonical patternmaker essay
  • Twelve-minute sketch-to-body film
  • Ten-frame “the missing middle” carousel
  • Five pattern-judgment shorts
  • Pattern Decision Ledger
  • Newsletter, fitting-room, classroom, and archive editions

Finished platform treatments

01

LONG VIDEO — Place sketch and finished dress at opposite ends, then refuse the jump cut. Walk through brief, block, pattern, toile, fitting, revision, grade, production file, and archive—with a named decision-maker at every supported step.

02

SHORT 01 — “A pattern is geometry with consequences.” Show how one line changes balance, movement, material consumption, construction, and fit.

03

SHORT 02 — “Do not credit the invisible specialist by guessing.” Find the record, ask the contributor, mark the unknown, and preserve the correction route.

04

CAROUSEL — THE SKETCH / THE BRIEF / THE BLOCK / THE FIRST PATTERN / THE TOILE / THE FIT / THE REVISION / THE GRADE / THE PRODUCTION FILE / THE CREDIT.

05

NEWSLETTER — Subject: Who made the sketch possible to wear? Use FIT’s patternmaking record to show skilled translation while keeping employment, ownership, and authorship claims case-specific.

06

FITTING ROOM EDITION — A live decision log with garment version, issue, wearer observation, proposed change, authority, approval, downstream effect, and archival note.

By RN Collins · Publication candidate v1.0 · 7 September 2026. Editorial, evidence, rights, accessibility, and production architecture are complete. Reading protocol

Every material statement carries an evidence label and point-of-claim source links. Interpretation is never presented as source fact. Legal sections identify their jurisdiction; state, foreign, contractual, beneficial-ownership, validity, priority, and disputed-fact questions remain counsel-review gates. This exhibition is educational and does not provide legal, conservation, or business advice.
